newsitem.title: USA: Israel to buy U.S. military helicopters.
newsitem.headline: Israel to buy U.S. military helicopters.

text.p: The Pentagon notified Congress on Wednesday that Israel plans to buy 15 U.S. UH-60L Blackhawk military helicopters and 34 helicopter engines for an estimated $200 million.

Sale of the troop-carrying helicopters, made by United Technology Corp's Sikorsky Aircraft division, and the General Electric Co. engines are part of Washington's continuing effort to assure Israeli military superiority in the Middle East.

Israel already has a number of Blackhawks in its military, the Pentagon noted in an announcement one day before Israeli Defense Minister Yitzhak Mordechai will visit the Defense Department for talks with Defense Secretary William Cohen.

"The sale will contribute to the foreign policy and national security of the United States by helping to improve the security of a friendly country which has been, and continues to be, an important force for political stability and economic progress in the Middle East," the Pentagon said.
The announcement did not say how Israel would pay for the helicopters, but such a large transfer could be made as part of annual U.S. military aid to Israel.

Jordan's King Hussein, meanwhile, held talks with Cohen at the Pentagon on Wednesday on growing military cooperation between Washington and Jordan, which has strongly supported the Middle East peace process and is anxious to improve its military forces.
